title: Residual fibre identification and Cohen–Macaulay tensor ring
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a locally finite type morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and $g:S'\to S$ any morphism. Put $X'=X\times_SS'$ with its projections $g':X'\to X$, $f':X'\to S'$ [def-pc-base-change]. Fix $r'\in S'$, set $r=g(r')$, $k=\kappa(r)$ and $k'=\kappa(r')$ [def-weil-residue-field], and form the fibres $Y=X_r$, $Y'=X'_{r'}$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Let $h:Y'\to Y$ be the canonical morphism induced by the fibre square, and let $z\in X$ satisfy $f(z)=r$, with canonical point $\bar z\in Y$. The residue field $\kappa_Y(\bar z)$ is canonically isomorphic to $\kappa_X(z)$ over $k$, and $\kappa_X(z)/k$ is finitely generated as a field [def-pc-field-extension]: $\kappa_X(z)=k(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ for finitely many elements, with no assumption that $z$ is closed. Put $T=k'\otimes_k\kappa_X(z)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with multiplication $(a\otimes b)(c\otimes d)=ac\otimes bd$. There is a canonical isomorphism $h^{-1}(\bar z)=Y'\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_Y(\bar z)\cong\operatorname{Spec}T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For each $z'\in X'$ over $z,r'$, this isomorphism identifies the canonical point over $z'$ in that fibre with the point of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ whose prime is the kernel of $T\to\kappa_{X'}(z')$, $a\otimes b\mapsto\bar a\bar b$, using the residue-field maps of the two projections. The ring $T$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and every prime localization $T_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a Noetherian local ring satisfying $\operatorname{depth}(T_{\mathfrak q})=\dim T_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-depth; def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

proof.text: Let $\iota:Y\to X$ and $\pi:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the fibre projections [def-pc-scheme-fibre], so $\iota(\bar z)=z$ and $f\circ\iota=j_r\circ\pi$ with $j_r:\operatorname{Spec}k\to S$ the canonical morphism. By [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient] (with $g=f$, $y=z$, $t=r$) the stalk map $\iota^\sharp_{\bar z}:\mathcal O_{X,z}\to\mathcal O_{Y,\bar z}$ is surjective with kernel $\mathfrak m_r\mathcal O_{X,z}$. A surjective local homomorphism of local rings maps the maximal ideal onto the maximal ideal, so the induced residue-field map $\varphi=\iota^\sharp:\kappa_X(z)\to\kappa_Y(\bar z)$ of $\iota$ [def-weil-residue-field] is surjective; being a field homomorphism it is injective, hence an isomorphism. Residue-field maps are functorial (they are induced by the stalk maps), so $f\circ\iota=j_r\circ\pi$ gives $\varphi\circ f^\sharp_z=\pi^\sharp_{\bar z}$ as maps $k\to\kappa_Y(\bar z)$, where $k$ is the residue field of the one point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and the fibre is a $k$-scheme through $\pi$. Thus $\varphi$ is the asserted canonical $k$-isomorphism, the residue-field map of $\iota$ itself and not an abstract isomorphism over $k$. This canonical choice matters in step 4: for $k=\mathbf Q$, $\kappa_X(z)=k'=\mathbf Q(i)$, twisting $\varphi$ by complex conjugation would exchange the two points of $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbf Q(i)\otimes_{\mathbf Q}\mathbf Q(i))$. Use $\varphi$ below.

source.place: Tag 01JT (lemma-points-fibre-product), applied to the defining fibre square $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(r)$; fibre stalk as quotient $\mathcal O_{X,z}/\mathfrak m_r\mathcal O_{X,z}$ (Tag 0HA1, via lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient).

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $r$. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], an affine member $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of its specified cover contains $z$, with $B=A[b_1,\ldots,b_n]$. Let $\mathfrak q$ represent $z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] the stalk at $z$ is $B_{\mathfrak q}$, compatibly with germs, so [lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra] identifies $\kappa_X(z)$ with $\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak q)$. The image of $A$ in this field lies in the image of $k=\kappa_S(r)$ by the residue-field map of $f$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Thus every element of $B/\mathfrak q$ is a polynomial in the images $\bar b_i$ with coefficients in $k$. Every element of its fraction field is a quotient of two such polynomials. Consequently $\kappa_X(z)\subseteq k(\bar b_1,\ldots,\bar b_n)$, and the reverse inclusion holds because $k$ and all $\bar b_i$ lie in $\kappa_X(z)$. This proves finite generation as a field without requiring $\mathfrak q$ maximal.

source.place: Tag 05DC (lemma-base-change-relative-assassin), second paragraph: finite-type hypothesis needed for Tag 045M; expanded using finite-type affine charts and the residue-field fraction description.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change], $Y'=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ with its canonical projections. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] now identifies $Y'\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_Y(\bar z)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}k'\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_Y(\bar z)$: a map into either side is exactly a pair of maps into these two field spectra whose composites to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ agree. The maps in both directions retain these two projections; their composites are identities by uniqueness. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] with $R=k$, $A=k'$, $B=\kappa_Y(\bar z)$, then step 1. This gives $h^{-1}(\bar z)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(k'\otimes_k\kappa_X(z))$, with projections induced by the two tensor inclusions.

source.place: Tag 05DC (lemma-base-change-relative-assassin), second paragraph, displayed residual fibre; affine product formula Tag 01I4 (schemes-lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes).

proof.text: For $z'$ as in the statement, naturality [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] makes its canonical residue-field point compatible with both projections $g',f'$. It therefore lifts to the fibre $Y'$, and then to $h^{-1}(\bar z)$ by [def-pc-fibre-product], with second component $\operatorname{Spec}(g'^\sharp\circ\varphi^{-1}):\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_{X'}(z')\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_Y(\bar z)$, where $\varphi=\iota^\sharp$ is the canonical isomorphism of step 1: the two composites into $Y=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}k$ agree after $\iota$ by naturality of $\iota$ at $\bar z$ and of $g'$ at $z'$, and after $\pi$ because both are $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the residue map $k\to\kappa_{X'}(z')$. Under step 3, the two component maps of this lift are precisely the residue-field maps $k'\to\kappa_{X'}(z')$ and $\kappa_X(z)\to\kappa_{X'}(z')$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] identifies its ring map with $a\otimes b\mapsto\bar a\bar b$. The kernel is the prime attached to $z'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field], applied to the original square $X\times_SS'$ (and exchanging the tensor factors). This is also the prime of its image in $\operatorname{Spec}T$: the unique prime $(0)$ in the spectrum of the target field pulls back to the kernel. This proves the point compatibility for the same scheme isomorphism, not merely a bijection of underlying sets.

source.place: Tag 01JT (lemma-points-fibre-product), proof: the prime is the kernel of the canonical tensor map; Tag 05DC residual-fibre identification.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-tensor-fields-cohen-macaulay] with $K=k'$ and $L=\kappa_X(z)$. The second extension is finitely generated by step 2; the theorem requires only one extension to be finitely generated and imposes no separability condition. Its tensor multiplication is exactly the multiplication specified for $T$. It gives Noetherianity of $T$ and, for every prime $\mathfrak q$, Noetherianity and locality of $T_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\operatorname{depth}(T_{\mathfrak q})=\dim T_{\mathfrak q}$, as required.
